summary: An estate agency or private property office: search and browse homes for sale or rent, a page per listing with gallery, facts, location and an enquiry, plus the agents, local area guides and a valuation request for sellers. Covers an everyday city agency with a list/map search and a luxury office that shows a small collection as large photographs and floor plans.

pages.purpose: Let buyers and renters start searching at once, show the best current homes, and give sellers a reason to request a valuation.

Luxury office: full-bleed slow crossfade of residences with a chapter list, a pause button (WCAG 2.2.2) and arrow keys; no autoplay or drift under reduced motion.

content: Every listing: reference, deal type, area, rooms, net/gross size, floor, build year, price or 'on request', description, features, daylight photos with alt text, map position, responsible agent, listed date
Areas covered, with average asking prices and their source and period (for guides)
Agents: name, role, areas, languages, portrait, direct phone
Commission terms and who pays them, if published
Agency licence or authorisation number and legal company name for the footer
Indicative mortgage rate with its date and a disclaimer (if the calculator is used)
Floor plans and room photos for premium listings (optional)
Office address, hours, phone, messaging number
One or two client quotes with permission

styles.name: bright city agency
styles.why: An everyday agency: a corporate sans for the interface with an italic serif for headings, warm amber accent, a glass search panel over photography.

styles.name: private office
styles.why: A luxury or off-market office: high-contrast didone headlines over a light geometric text face, deep muted accent, edge-to-edge photographs and dark photographic bands; motion is full but slow (long crossfades, curtain reveals, one scroll drift).

pitfalls: Listings without the legally required details (agency authorisation number, the owner's written authorisation to advertise, accurate size and price); some markets fine misleading listings.
Stale listings: sold or let homes left online; every listing needs a status and a listed date.
Empty or generic photo alt text; describe each room.
Showing the exact address or unit of an occupied home without the owner's consent.
A mortgage calculator that reads like a credit offer; label it indicative and date the rate.
Map-only interfaces: pins must be keyboard buttons and every listing also reachable in the list.
Autoplaying hero films without a pause control and without a reduced-motion fallback.
Area price figures without a source and period.
